Hi, coaches. I can't wait for this next presentation, Martin Rocker. Martin is a world-class highly innovative specialist in the area of blue to green ball coaching. Join us today as Martin takes us through the pathway to the yellow ball. Hello, friends. I'm Martin Rocker. Welcome to my presentation. I want to thank Tennis Australia for the invitation once again to this conference. I'm thrilled and honored to be part of this lineup surrounded by amazing professionals. What I want to show you is the way I work with little kids. I've been coaching for 32 years now. I'm from Buenos Aires, Argentina. I worked there for eight years and then I moved to New York for five years. Now I live in Spain in the Barcelona area and I've been here for almost two decades. So, grabbing ideas from different countries, different methodologies, that led to make me see the way I have to coach kids with a personal perspective. I call that mini players. It's like, you can call it philosophy or methodology, a system. I think it's the way I understand how we have to teach the kids in order to engage them and love the sport and practice it no matter what they are, if they're very skillful, if they're not, they have to learn how to play the sport and we have to get the best performance out of them. I see myself as a very technical coach. I want my kids to have proper technique, proper footwork, good positioning on the court, a good understanding of the game.

But we have to make it fun and also work on the electricity, work on the skills, work on their coordination because kids nowadays don't have the skills that kids had 30 years ago. Kids don't go out on the streets anymore. They don't play. They don't come up trees. They don't play by themselves because parents go too fanatic about safety and safety measures and if they ride a bike, they have to wear a helmet and pass all over the body because they don't want them to get hurt. What we have to do in the sessions is to work on coordination, work on the way they move their body. They understand how to use their body, how to use an implement like a tennis racket on a tennis ball.

And according to that, we are going to make them understand, enjoy the game and have fun but also improve their skills. What you see in this video is that you see kids three, four, five year olds in the same group doing the same tracks. Obviously, the goals that they have for each other are different. You have to adapt to their possibilities. Some of them will make it faster. Some of them will take more time to do it but you have to ask them to do what they can, not more than that. Obviously, you have to challenge them sometimes but the thing is to maintain them doing activities all the time. Always active, always in motion and reproducing mechanics that they wouldn't do when they play tennis. Also, if you play games with them, try to engage them in team competitions because if you challenge them and they reach the goal, they consider as a team victory. This way, every player will feel important. As you can see in my sessions, every ball counts. So you don't see loose balls on the ground. Every time they push the ball or they hit the ball, there's someone waiting for the ball to be hit. It's either a coach, it's either a teammate. Sometimes they try to hit a cone but every ball counts, it's important for them to understand that they cannot hit the ball hard and out of control. So every time they hit it, there's someone waiting for it. As I was saying before, and you can see it now, every time they hit, there's a target for them.
